ROME · OCT 2027

Three nights in Rome, with the markets as good as the ruins.

Trastevere on the first night, the Colosseum and Forum on timed tickets, then the Vatican and Trionfale Market. Sunday is Porta Portese flea market before an evening flight home. Book the Colosseum and the Vatican first: official tickets release 30 days out.

Thu, Day 1Nightlife
Arrive, Trastevere by night.
  • Settle in
  • Trastevere evening — cobbled lanes, trattorie, the piazza at Santa Maria in Trastevere
Fri, Day 2Culture
Colosseum & the Forum, then Testaccio.
  • Colosseum + Roman Forum, no closing day but timed-entry only MUST-SEE BOOK AHEAD — official tickets release exactly 30 days out at 9am Rome time, so mark the date
  • Testaccio Market, afternoon — locals outnumber tourists, best 9–11am Mon–Sat, closed Sun
Sat, Day 3Culture
Vatican & Trionfale Market.
  • Vatican Museums, Sistine Chapel — closed Sundays except the free last Sunday of the month (avoid that day, it's packed) MUST-SEE BOOK AHEAD; St Peter's is free entry but the dome climb needs its own ticket, and the basilica closes Wed mornings for the papal audience
  • Trionfale Market, 10 min walk away, one of Rome's best food-market experiences — good lunch stop Mon–Sat, closed Sun
  • Trevi Fountain & the Pantheon, evening walk
Sun, Day 4Markets
Porta Portese & a slow morning.
  • Porta Portese flea market Sun only, ~7am–2pm — the one day this giant flea market runs, and it happens to be departure day
  • Evening flight home from FCO

Campo de' Fiori's market is Mon–Sat and closed Sunday, so it doesn't work on a Sunday departure — Porta Portese is the better fit for this exact day.

Festivals & Events

  • LIKELYFesta del Cinema di Roma — ~Oct 13–24, this stay should catch its closing days.
  • FIXEDRomaeuropa Festival — runs Sept–mid Nov, covers the entire stay.
  • No Italian public holidays fall during this stay (Oct 21–24) — normal opening hours throughout.

Rome's film festival should be closing out right around this stay — 2026 is confirmed for Oct 14–25, so 2027 landing in the Oct 21–24 window is a good bet for at least its final days.

Fun fact

Tourists throw around €3,000 a day into the Trevi Fountain — over €1 million a year. Rome collects it every morning and hands it to Caritas Roma, which puts it toward a food bank and soup kitchen for people in need across the city.
